AC-3 says a document that is not an open ticket document gets no diagnostic. didClose publishes an empty list for any opened file whose path only has the shape `.stapel/tickets/<X>/ticket.md` (locate_path does not read the disk). Case: a `ticket.md` in folder `-x`, or in a folder with no `stapel.toml` or `state.json`, is opened and closed. The server publishes `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` with `[]` for it. The test `nothing_for_other_documents` does not send didClose, so it would not fail.

AC-11 says a body or text of more than 5000 lines gives no hints, with one logMessage. The code counts lines after dropping the blank lines at the edges of each side (`counted`). A body of 5003 lines with 3 blank edge lines still gets hints, although the criterion counts the lines of the body. The code also sends the warning (type WARNING) on every refresh: every keystroke, save and button run repeats the message for the same buffer. This is the open DR1-4/CR1-3 item. No test covers the repeat or the edge-blank rule.

AC-12 says the diagnostics of every open ticket.md are published again when a button run ends. The code refreshes only on the path where `run_button` ran. The `could not run` path of `run_button` also reaches the refresh, which matches the text. The two refusals (agent shell, page not current) do not refresh, and AC-12 does not ask for it. The ok refusal after a changed page shows nothing new on the client. No drift, but the case where `stapel ok` runs and exits nonzero (a partial confirm) is not tested for the refresh. `diagnostics_after_ok` covers only the success case.

The 5000-line warning (DR1-4) is still sent through `window/logMessage` on every refresh, so on every keystroke (didChange) while a section is over the limit. Failing case: a 6000-line waiting body that gets a didChange per edit fills the client log with the same warning. AC-11 asks for 'one window/logMessage' and the dedupe that `sent.bad` gives for AC-13 errors is missing.

Time-of-check to time-of-use gap on `stapel.ok`: the server checks `current_page` and the offered hash, then `run_button` starts the child `stapel ok KEY`. The child does not receive or re-check the hash. If `page.md` or `ticket.md` changes in that interval, the child confirms against the new state. The window is narrow because the server is single-threaded, but another process can still change the files in it.

`run_button` blocks the server loop in `Command::output()` with no timeout. A hung child, for example `stapel next` waiting on a lock, stops all replies, including `shutdown` and `exit`. The ticket's Not promised list covers a second run during a run, but not a hung one.

XR1-5 is patched only in part. The Test plan row 'Review round 1 coverage' lists 'a run whose child prints nothing: done' under save_refreshes_diagnostics, refusals_beyond_the_first_cases and ok_refused_after_a_reloaded_page, but none of them, and no other test in lsp.rs, checks the 'stapel <args>: done' form or the bare 'stapel <args>: exit <n>' form of AC-4. Failing case: change run_button to show '{label}: ' or '{label}: exit {n}: ' when there is no first line, and every test stays green. Also, the External states row 'child process | ... output with non-UTF-8 bytes' still names lsp::runs_a_button and lsp::a_failing_button, while the Review Focus says that case is not tested.

XR1-4 is closed only for the save handler, not for the capability. initialize_and_shutdown asserts only textDocumentSync.change (or the bare 1). Removing save: Some(TextDocumentSyncSaveOptions::Supported(true)) or open_close: Some(true) from capabilities() leaves every test green, because the test client sends didOpen and didSave without looking at the capabilities. A real client such as Zed then sends no didSave (and, under the LSP default, may send no open or close), so the AC-10 refresh on save never happens.

Some test references in the Spec name tests that do not hold their case. (1) The Abuse row 'edits ticket.md and runs stapel page after the button was offered' names only ok_refused_after_the_page_changed; that test's regenerated-page case sends no didChange, so it is refused because the buffer differs from the disk, not because of the hash. ok_refused_after_a_reloaded_page reaches the hash check but is not named. (2) The Inputs row for the arguments of 'stapel lsp' names initialize_and_shutdown; the exit 2 case is in refusals_beyond_the_first_cases. (3) The Agent shell row claims 'stapel.ok on a current page' for each variable in refuses_in_an_agent_shell; that test uses the non-current page, and the current-page case exists only for CLAUDECODE, in refusals_beyond_the_first_cases.

AC-5 says bad arguments get InvalidParams with 'stapel lsp: the arguments must be the URI of an open ticket.md or page.md', and that this check comes first. When ExecuteCommandParams does not deserialize (for example 'arguments': 'x', or no 'command' field), the server answers InvalidParams with the serde error text instead. No test sends such parameters.

AC-11 says a body of more than 5000 lines gives one window/logMessage, but changed_lines pushes the Warning on every refresh, so each didChange of a long section logs again. The test sends only one change. Also, the limit counts lines without the blank lines at the edges of each side, which is not what 'a body of more than 5000 lines' says.

Two branches of AC-10 and AC-13 have no test. (1) AC-10 'its folder stops being a key', the Ok(None) path from key_number: diagnostics_cleared_when_the_state_goes covers only the legacy Ok(None). (2) AC-13 'a stapel.toml that is missing': nothing_for_other_documents opens the bare root but does not check for the Error log line.

The pack's base 6c6e27b is older than the merge of main (4df5d82), so diff.patch holds all of STP-38, and the deletion check for this ticket cannot be done from the diff alone. Proposal: stapel review start should take the merge-base with main's current head as the base.

didClose publishes an empty list for any opened path of the form .stapel/tickets/<X>/ticket.md (it uses locate_path), including the folder '-x' and folders without state.json, which AC-3 says get no diagnostic. nothing_for_other_documents never closes a document, so it does not see this.

Each code action request on page.md runs prepare_waiting, which reads the branch through git, and computes page_text. Editors ask for code actions on cursor moves, so a git process is started per move. Proposal: cache by the mtimes of page.md, ticket.md and state.json.
